objections.claim: The new `recoverLabelled` step scans the ENTIRE output for a label line and takes the JSON after it, with no requirement that the label sit in a fence or near the start of the output. The eval prompts embed untrusted material (spec text, diff, context files — the same channel `review-call.mjs` already flags as injectable, see the FAFF-990 comment on untrusted diff echoed into findings). If the model omits its own judgement but echoes a context snippet containing `faff-eval:judgement` on its own line followed by a JSON object with the expected `case_id` (knowable to an attacker who can write the spec/issue text, since the case id is derived from the ticket), the injected object is recovered as the rep's judgement. The `expectedCaseId` check does not help: the attacker's payload carries the matching id precisely because it was planted in the prompt that contains it. The pre-existing `ANY_FENCE` fallback has the same shape but at least requires a fenced block; this step removes even that delimiter, so a bare label line anywhere in streamed deliberation or quoted context suffices.
objections.evidence: Spec §4 Pattern 1, `recoverLabelled` steps 2–3 ("Find every index i where lines[i] matches …" / "body = lines after i … to end of text"); `eval/envelope.mjs` fallback contract; the spec's own Reference context notes the parser is eval-only, which bounds the blast radius to eval integrity, not production gating.
objections.predicted_consequence: A planted payload in a spec or issue body can supply a forged eval judgement (e.g. `findings: []`) for a rep whose model emitted no judgement, corrupting `format_adherence`/accuracy measurements for exactly the non-Claude models this ticket is trying to measure — silently, since the record is flagged only `noncompliant`, which is also what honest mis-tags produce. Cheap in-place hardening: require the label line to be the first non-blank line of the output (or within the first N lines), matching where a real near-miss emission actually lands.
objections.disposition_rationale: label recovery anchored to the first non-blank line (one stray empty fence allowed); a label further down is not recovered

objections.claim: The ticket's own description still lists the fourth observed pattern (empty HTTP 200 completions) and its expected outcome ("the cause is identified, and either fixed or surfaced"), but the spec moves that work to FAFF-1228. The slice as captured promises more than it ships, so the pipeline's value/expectation record and the delivered increment disagree.
objections.evidence: The methodology critique's "Deps surfaced?" section: "the issue description still lists pattern 4 and its expected outcome … which this ticket no longer delivers. What to do: add a one-line scope pointer at the top of the description naming the spec and FAFF-1228." The spec's own OUT OF SCOPE section confirms pattern 4 is excluded.
objections.predicted_consequence: A reviewer or tracker consumer reading the issue expects the empty-completion pattern to be fixed or surfaced by this ticket; when it ships without that, the outcome is recorded as unmet or the gap is rediscovered downstream instead of being visible at capture time.
objections.disposition_rationale: scope pointer added to the issue description naming the spec and FAFF-1228

objections.claim: The critique judges `complex` too high for the post-split scope — two parser fallbacks, four one-sentence brief edits, tests, and one scoped gate run — and recommends re-tiering to `standard`. Shipping at `complex` misprices the increment for the pipeline.
objections.evidence: The methodology critique's "Right-sized?" section: "With pattern 4 moved to FAFF-1228, the `complex` tier looks high for what is left. `standard` would match the scope … What to do: consider re-tiering to `standard`." The spec's contract block still records `build-tier: complex`.
objections.predicted_consequence: not separately stated — the critique itself frames this as "consider", so it is a taste-level pricing concern, not a defect that blocks the slice.
objections.disposition_rationale: build-tier is the CLI deterministic faff tier output (complex after the split); not hand-edited
